summary: Tested 3 major features + regression for ORCA: (1) route polyline visibility + sea-not-land fix, (2) Alerts tab 'Marine Situation & Alert Intelligence Center' redesign, (3) Voice Agent (ElevenLabs). Backend: 8/8 pytest cases passed including the critical /api/voice/speak returning valid audio/mpeg (CONFIRMED working end-to-end, not mocked), /api/voice/transcribe correctly returns 200/422 (no 401/402/503 credential errors) for a synthetic silent WAV, /api/situation returns correct deterministic severity (kakinada=CRITICAL due to active high-severity 'Cyclone Warning - Deep Depression BOB-04' alert even with SAFE weather verdict; mumbai=WARNING), and route_safety chat intent returns a connected route_line layer + route_start/route_end markers + names the hazard ('Chennai Port Restricted Zone') in the synthesized text with verdict UNSAFE. Frontend (mobile viewport 375x667): chat map widget shows connected colored polyline info (web fallback list with color-coded dots, ROUTE banner, START(white)/DESTINATION(blue) markers, hazard names+coords) for the Kakinada->Hope Island query; sea-shift verified (start marker at 82.2700 lon vs Kakinada center 82.2475 lon, shifted east into the bay water, ~2.5km); Alerts tab verified for kakinada (CRITICAL, red radar sweep) and mumbai (WARNING, amber radar sweep) with animated rotating radar confirmed via multiple screenshots showing different sweep angles; Active Hazards/Notifications lists show CRITICAL/WARNING severity badges correctly; language switch EN->TE works app-wide (via Chat tab's global language picker, testID=lang-option-te) with clean Telugu glyph rendering on both Chat and Alerts tab titles/badges/labels with no layout breakage; mic-button and listen-button testIDs both present and functional (listen-button tap did not crash the app on web preview). No console errors or backend 500s observed during any test.

issues: Localization gap: the 'reasons' list text (e.g. 'Wind, wave and lightning conditions are within safe limits.') and tide type label ('High'/'Low') come verbatim from the backend's deterministic rules.py/mock_region.py and are NEVER translated even when app language is switched to Telugu/Hindi - confirmed visually, English sentence remained in an otherwise fully-Telugu-rendered Alerts screen. This partially violates review point 2(f) ('language switch updates all new Alerts-tab text correctly'). Not a crash/blocker, just incomplete localization coverage for this one card.

design_issues.screen: Alerts tab - SituationCard (severity vs reasons mismatch)
issues: When severity is CRITICAL purely due to an active high-severity alert (not today's weather verdict, e.g. Kakinada cyclone bulletin for +36h while today's verdict is SAFE), the reasons list under the CRITICAL badge still only says 'Wind, wave and lightning conditions are within safe limits' with no mention of the cyclone/why it's CRITICAL - could read as contradictory to a user glancing at just the card (badge=CRITICAL, text=safe). The cycloneBanner only triggers off weather_today.cyclone, not off an alert-driven severity bump, so no visual cue ties the CRITICAL badge to its actual cause on this card (the cause is only visible after scrolling to Active Hazards).

action_items: LOW: Consider localizing rule-generated 'reasons' strings and tide type labels (High/Low) via the t() translation helper, or move them into the same LLM-explained text so TE/HI users get a fully native-language card.

LOW: Consider surfacing the alert-driven cause (e.g. cyclone name) inline on SituationCard when severity is CRITICAL/WARNING due to an alert rather than today's weather verdict, so the badge and body text never appear to contradict each other at a glance.
No blocking issues found. Voice /api/voice/speak is CONFIRMED working end-to-end (real ElevenLabs audio returned, not mocked) - safe to consider that credential saga fully resolved.
critical_code_review_comments: voice/service.py: clean separation of STT/TTS from the orchestrator, graceful fallback from eleven_v3->eleven_multilingual_v2 for non-Telugu, VoiceUnavailable exception pattern keeps chat flow safe from voice failures - well structured.

orchestrator/agents.py planner prompt: the 'ROUTE COORDINATES - CRITICAL' instruction block is clear and correctly reasoned (LLM-based shift, not deterministic) - verified in testing it does shift the point off the literal city-center coordinate in the correct direction (out to sea), though magnitude is prompt-dependent/non-deterministic as expected.
rules.py compute_situation_severity: clean, deterministic, correctly prioritizes critical>warning>advisory from either the weather verdict OR alert severity - matches spec exactly.
SituationCard.tsx: reasons/tide text sourced directly from backend without passing through t()/localization - see design_issues above.

success_rate.backend: 100% (8/8 pytest cases: voice/speak, voice/speak-validation, voice/transcribe, situation x2 regions, situation-severity-cyclone, route-safety chat x2)
success_rate.frontend: All requested checks passed: route map widget + sea-shift + hazard naming, Alerts redesign (situation card, animated radar, 3 trend charts, hazards/notifications with severity badges) across 2 regions, EN->TE language switch across Chat+Alerts, mic-button/listen-button present and non-crashing. 2 minor localization/UX polish gaps noted above.

seed_data_creation: None - reused existing seeded mock regions (kakinada, mumbai) and their pre-seeded alerts/geofence data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 3 major features from this session (route polyline+sea-fix, Alerts redesign, Voice Agent) are working end-to-end on both backend and web-preview frontend. ElevenLabs voice/speak is CONFIRMED live (real mp3 bytes returned) - the credential saga mentioned in the context note is resolved. Native mic recording/audio playback on Expo Go/simulator was NOT tested (sandbox limitation, as expected) - only backend voice endpoints + frontend button presence/no-crash were verified per the review request's own scoping. Two minor, non-blocking localization polish items remain (rule-generated English strings on SituationCard not translated; CRITICAL badge cause not visually tied to alert when it's alert-driven rather than weather-driven) - fine to defer or fix opportunistically.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no blocking bugs found this pass. The two design_issues above are polish/completeness gaps, not functional bugs: rules.py/mock_region.py generate plain English strings server-side that SituationCard renders verbatim without routing through the t() i18n helper used elsewhere in the same component.
